articleSummary: As of June 7, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reached 515 confirmed cases and 91 deaths, resulting in a case fatality rate of 17.6%. The majority of infections are concentrated in Ituri province, particularly in Mongbwalu, which accounts for over 94% of cases. This outbreak is associated with the Bundibugyo strain, for which no approved vaccines or treatments are available. The World Health Organization (WHO) has declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, warning that without immediate intervention, cases could exceed 20,000. A $518 million response plan has been initiated, with emergency supplies being airlifted to Bunia. Additionally, Uganda has reported 19 confirmed cases linked to the outbreak, raising concerns about cross-border transmission. Local authorities are implementing strict measures to limit social gatherings, while community engagement and early care seeking are deemed critical for controlling the outbreak. The situation is further complicated by ongoing conflict and distrust in health systems, which hinder effective reporting and containment.
